title: Replaceable desktop, core and worker boundaries
context: The workbench needs close human-AI collaboration with independently replaceable UI, core and computation responsibilities.
authority: The owner's engineering contract and subsequent product clarifications.
consequences: Cross-language contracts and failure handling require executable checks.
Runtime boundary changes follow the engineering contract's decision policy.
history_note: Common record metadata was added when repository continuity was established. No unrecorded historical alternative evaluation is inferred.
decision: Keep the specified React/TypeScript, Rust/Tauri 2, controlled Python worker architecture.
selection_policy: Evaluate architecture by human–AI financial collaboration needs, replaceability, and operational fit. Complexity must serve a concrete need; minimizing resource footprint is not a mandatory objective. Reuse suitable external or shared capabilities, and build focused local implementations when requirements or lifetime costs justify them.
evolution: Each adapter can be replaced or removed behind a small versioned contract.
Add abstract ports when the first use case needs them; do not create unused framework layers.
New asset classes are data, not closed enums.
Version external protocols and persistent formats; internal code may be rewritten.
Use migration and contract fixtures as rewrite checks, not implementation-specific tests.
Current stack choices are revisable decisions, not permanent product requirements.
revisit_when: Measured UI or process costs fail the performance target.
A provider requires a different isolation or integration boundary.
